contract: One human verification decision belongs to one peer connection. Both devices must independently confirm the same authenticated session/transcript before file metadata or payload are exposed; stale messages/closed or replaced sessions must never authorize a new connection. Malformed control input must fail closed. Retrying pairing must preserve prepared source data while requiring fresh connection authorization.
claim: The confirmation gate appears to scope each human decision to its connection and gate metadata/payload; this is an interim claim to scrutinize, not release acceptance.
whyItMatters: An authorization lifecycle error could send filenames or data to an unintended peer.

reviewer.scope: Static authorization module, production callers, transcript/parsing and existing tests

crossModel: Skipped: non-interactive autonomous goal continuation; no external review CLI invoked.

parentChecks: Transcript session and exact SDP binding in webrtc-signaling.ts
Strict peer-confirmed parsing and fail-closed callback paths
Receiver checks before queued metadata/payload work
Connection generation checks and close/reset on teardown
Sender manifest emission requires both confirmations and prepared source
reconciliation.decision: No concrete issue to reproduce or fix in this scoped static pass. Do not treat absence of findings as completion of wrong-device security acceptance.

stopCondition: One fresh-context cycle, no substantive finding; no repeated review loop.
scope: Partial static evidence only. Physical wrong-device/operator verification, all other threat paths and final release adversarial pass remain open.
